title: Plus-Sized Elf
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Massage therapist Naoe treats Elfuda, an elf who got fat on French fries during her stay on Earth and must slim down to fit back through the portal home. Each chapter brings another overweight mythical woman (a dark elf, a merrow, an ogre and more) to his clinic for diet, exercise and massage, in an ecchi comedy with real stretching routines (Wikipedia; ANN; Seven Seas blurb via AniList).
life_message: Getting healthy takes steady habits and a supportive helper, and it is a personal choice.

content.note: Seductive fan-service poses and a near-nude chapter (ANN); therapist's 'chubby chaser' fetish and harem dreams (Wikipedia); MU Borderline H, Nudity; AniList Nudity 68.
Body jokes such as 'chubby chasers' and 'chocolate' for dark-elf skin (ANN).
Binge drinking shown as comedy (ANN); an ogre's beer belly and a manager who drinks often (Wikipedia).
Weight shame and body image; reviewers split on whether it shames its cast (ANN); MU Weight Gain, Diet.
Crash dieting played for laughs (ANN); exercise and massage how-tos included (ANN; AniList Educational 79).
Junk food (French fries) as the running cause (Wikipedia).

dominant: Fitness and diet comedy; fan service; body image

frames.aligns: Naoe never shames clients and helps them toward health (ANN); temperance against gluttony.
frames.concerns: Women framed in seductive, near-nude fan service; borderline-hentai art (MU).
Heavy fan service, nudity and binge drinking.
Nudity, sexual content and magic beings.

frames.aligns: Range of body types and a non-shaming helper (ANN).
frames.concerns: Exploitative fan service and dark-skin jokes (ANN).
Nudity, sexual fan service and alcohol throughout.

frames.aligns: Craving for junk food overcome by mindful habits.
Some body-type diversity and health information.
frames.concerns: Sexualization, fatphobia debate and a skin-color joke (ANN).
Immorality in images and magic beings.

frames.aligns: Freedom from limiting beliefs about the body.
frames.concerns: Focus on bodily flaws and sensuality.

frames.aligns: Bodily autonomy and choice in health.
Bodies and pleasure seen positively; nature beings.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Elf and dark-elf rivalry is comic, not violent (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Diet regimens versus indulgence; getting healthy a personal choice (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clinic clients, not families, form the cast.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Therapist and clients as equals; workplace manager (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Nutrition and exercise science over fantasy origins (ANN).

folkways.japan: Seitai osteopathic massage and the 'reverse isekai' of fantasy beings in modern Japan are Japanese settings; diet comedy reflects Japanese beauty norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN: exercise routines and health facts are spelled out with instructions; reviewers split on whether it mocks or helps its cast.
delivery.note: Health advice is stated directly in teaching segments, while the comedy and fan service pull in another direction.

winners_losers: Clients slim down, often only to regain weight; Naoe keeps helping. Sympathy is mixed between the women and the comedy at their expense.
